first_page:
Fundamental limits in photonics and
electromagnetics: a tutorial
Owen D. Miller1 and Francesco Monticone2
1Yale, owen.miller@yale.edu
2Cornell, francesco.monticone@cornell.edu
May 26, 2026
Abstract
Theoretical limits and physical bounds across many areas of science, mathe-
matics, and technology—including Shannon’s information-capacity limits, Bennett
and Landauer’s thermodynamic limits on computation, and Gödel’s incompleteness
theorem in formal logic—serve as defining pillars of their fields. In photonics and
electromagnetism, numerous physical bounds and constraints have likewise been un-
covered over the past several decades. In this Tutorial, we first review the fundamental
principles that constrain light-matter interactions, and then discuss limits at different
hierarchical scales, from optical material responses to wave propagation, scattering,
and related optical phenomena and functions, relevant to a wide range of applications.
